knowledge_abstraction.bug_theme: Zero-dimensional parameter shape violation during model replication
knowledge_abstraction.general_principle: Parameter transformation utilities may produce non-standard parameter shapes, and subsequent model replication or device transition logic may assume parameters have at least one dimension.

risk_dimensions.shape: Zero-dimensional or scalar parameter shapes produced by normalization utilities
risk_dimensions.device: Multi-device execution through parallel replication wrappers
risk_dimensions.execution_state: Model replication and forward/backward execution after parameter shape transformation

failure_mechanism.description: Model replication logic may not correctly handle zero-dimensional parameters generated by parameter transformation APIs, causing exceptions or inconsistent behavior during multi-device execution.

input_exploration: Explore modules with parameter transformation utilities that can generate zero-dimensional or scalar parameters
Vary parameter shape boundaries and observe behavior under model replication
Combine non-standard parameter shapes with multi-device execution
constraint_awareness: Requires a multi-device environment to trigger replication-related failures
Parallel wrappers may contain hidden assumptions about parameter dimensionality
Single-device and multi-device behavior should be compared
oracle_strategy: Catch exceptions during model replication or forward/backward execution
Compare multi-device execution results against single-device reference behavior

transferability.reason: The principle applies to any API that changes parameter structure or creates degenerate parameter shapes, especially when combined with model replication or device transitions.

important_considerations: Probe parameter shape boundaries created by normalization-style utilities
Test under parallel replication wrappers on multiple devices
Exercise both forward and backward execution paths
generation_strategy: Generate harnesses that apply parameter-shape-transforming utilities to small modules, wrap them with parallel replication wrappers, run forward and backward execution on multiple devices, and monitor for exceptions or divergence from single-device behavior.
